newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican spot peso closes 1.15 centavos firmer.
newsitem.headline: Mexican spot peso closes 1.15 centavos firmer.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderated some of its early advances against the dollar towards the close Monday as domestic brokers chose to acquire positions in dollars again, currency traders said.
"First of all dollars were in supply until the same-day market closed, and then there was some demand from domestic banks to repurchase positions," a peso trader said.
The 24-hour and 48-hour peso closed 1.55 and 1.15 centavos firmer at 7.5375/7.5425 and 7.54/7.5485 per dollar, respectively.
The 24-hour and 48-hour peso at their most firm traded at 7.5280/7.5380 and 7.5320/7.5420 per dollar, respectively, in early trade.

Some traders said that the peso benefitted early on from foreign investors entering the secondary money market to take advantage of rates available before an expected drop in primary rates at Tuesday's central bank auction.
Traders estimated that the benchmark 28-day Cetes rate could fall by over 100 basis points from its current primary level of 25.47 percent.
The same-day peso closed 2.6 centavos firmer earlier at 7.5340/7.5380 per dollar.
